description: Capture the AFTER evidence and prove the WS2 acceptance criteria with numbers + images, not adjectives. Depends on FEAT-002. Re-run the fixed-camera screenshot harness and the frame-time harness (from FEAT-001) for all four scenes and record: BEFORE/AFTER fixed-camera screenshots per scene showing improved lighting/shadows/material depth; Fast-path frame time before vs after (must show NO regression) AND High-path frame time; per-scene confirmation of no avatar skin/face highlight blow-out (with the chef and wardrobe avatars visible in the AFTER shots); and, for any scene whose tone mapping changed, the per-scene justification screenshot. Also record cold-load byte deltas to prove the WS1 budget was not blown and note any asset added with its size.
steps: With FEAT-002 built, run `npm run build`. Then capture AFTER fixed-camera screenshots for all four scene routes on BOTH quality paths (at least: High and Fast) via scripts/measure-load.mjs into docs/visual/ (e.g. --out docs/visual --label after-<scene>-high / after-<scene>-fast). The harness screenshots are animation-disabled and clipped to the canvas for deterministic comparison against BEFORE.

Capture AFTER frame-time readings for all four scenes on BOTH the Fast path and the High path using the FEAT-001 frame-time harness, into docs/visual/. Compare Fast AFTER vs the BEFORE (today) frame time per scene and confirm no regression (Fast >= as fast as today). Also report High-path frame time so the orchestrator can attach it.

For the wardrobe and chef scenes, ensure the AFTER (High) screenshots clearly show the avatar's face/skin so no blow-out can be verified visually. If FEAT-002 changed any scene's tone mapping, include the explicit per-scene before/after justification screenshot pair proving the change fixes (not causes) skin blow-out, referenced in the doc.

Re-run cold-load byte measurement (measure-load.mjs default byte report) for the four scene routes and compare totals to docs/perf/AFTER.md's WS1 numbers; record any delta and, if an environment map/texture asset was added in FEAT-002, its size. Confirm the WS1 cold-load byte budget is not blown.

Write docs/visual/AFTER.md: machine (Linux sandbox x86-64, software GL SwiftShader) + Node v22.23.2 + Chrome for Testing version + viewport 1280x900 dpr 1; a per-scene BEFORE->AFTER screenshot table (paths); a per-scene Fast-path frame-time before/after table + High-path frame time (median/mean/p95 ms + FPS) with the software-GL caveat; per-scene tone-mapping decision (unchanged ACESFilmic, or switched to Neutral@1.0 with the justification screenshot referenced); per-scene no-skin-blow-out confirmation; cold-load byte deltas + any asset added with size; and confirmation that exactly ONE shared High/Fast quality concept is used across all four scenes.

Do NOT commit out/, node_modules/, .next/, assets-src/. Commit the docs/visual/ AFTER artifacts + AFTER.md on branch visual/lighting-quality (e.g. `docs(visual): WS2 before/after screenshots + Fast/High frame-time evidence`).
acceptance_criteria: docs/visual/ contains AFTER fixed-camera screenshots for all four scenes (High and Fast), alongside the FEAT-001 BEFORE shots, showing improved lighting/shadows/material depth.
docs/visual/AFTER.md documents Fast-path frame time before vs after per scene showing NO regression, plus High-path frame time, with machine+browser+viewport stated and the software-GL caveat noted.
Per-scene no-skin-blow-out is confirmed with the chef and wardrobe avatars visible in the AFTER shots; any tone-mapping change is backed by a referenced per-scene justification screenshot.
Cold-load byte deltas are recorded and show the WS1 budget is not blown; any added asset is listed with its size (or 'none added' is stated).
AFTER.md confirms exactly ONE shared quality concept across all four scenes.
out/, node_modules/, .next/, assets-src/ are not committed; docs/perf/ is untouched.
verification: Confirm docs/visual/ holds before-* and after-* PNG + frame-time JSON for all four scenes and an AFTER.md.
Open AFTER.md and confirm it contains the Fast before/after + High frame-time numbers, the per-scene tone-mapping decisions, and the no-blow-out confirmations.
Run `git status --short` and confirm no out/, node_modules/, .next/, assets-src/ paths are staged and docs/perf/ files are unmodified.
findings:
DONE. Captured all AFTER evidence for WS2 and wrote docs/visual/AFTER.md. No scene/lighting behavior changed (this was evidence + docs only); the ONLY code change was a measurement-only --quality high|fast flag added to BOTH harness scripts (scripts/measure-load.mjs + scripts/measure-frametime.mjs). The flag clicks the shared QualityToggle radio (role=radio, name High/Fast) AFTER the canvas mounts to drive each render path deterministically; it changes no scene/quality rendering code and records the selected tier in each JSON. quality.ts had no localStorage/URL persistence (React state only), so clicking the existing toggle was the clean non-invasive path.

SCREENSHOTS (8): after-<scene>-high.png + after-<scene>-fast.png for coach/chef/wardrobe/pet, alongside FEAT-001 before-*.png. All ready=true, hasCanvas=true, unresolvedFailures=[]. NO-BLOW-OUT verified visually on the two skin-bearing avatars in the High shots: wardrobe VRM (after-wardrobe-high.png) face/cheeks/neck keep natural skin tone, no white roll-off; chef FBX (after-chef-high.png) forehead/nose/cheeks natural warm tone. Coach OBJ + pet fur also true-color. Improved lighting/depth clearly visible vs before (key/fill/bounce shaping + procedural ground disc on High).

FRAME TIME (Fast before->after median, NO REGRESSION on any scene): coach 83.3->83.3 (equal); chef 83.3->66.7 (faster); wardrobe 100.1->83.3 (faster); pet 250.0->183.3 (faster). Fast is at-least-as-cheap everywhere because Fast caps dpr [0.75,1.25] (< today's [1,2]) and disables the shadow map. High-path medians (expected opt-in cost): coach 83.4, chef 83.3, wardrobe 116.7, pet 300.0. Software-GL (SwiftShader) caveat documented; pet/wardrobe frame counts are low (17-43) so medians are the reliable signal, tails noisy. High p95 on pet (383.3) is actually below before p95 (516.6).

COLD-LOAD BYTES vs docs/perf/AFTER.md WS1: coach 2,440,696->2,459,762 (+19,066 B, +0.78%); chef 2,581,387->2,600,451 (+19,064 B, +0.74%); wardrobe 8,248,182->8,267,245 (+19,063 B, +0.23%); pet 9,854,000->9,873,067 (+19,067 B, +0.19%). Near-constant ~19KB is the shared quality.ts + QualityToggle.tsx JS on every route (byType shows .js growth, NO new .vrm/.glb/.hdr/image entry). NO ASSET ADDED (ground disc is procedural in-memory CanvasTexture). WS1 budget not blown (all <1%).

TONE MAPPING (CONSTRAINT #2): ALL FOUR UNCHANGED = THREE.ACESFilmicToneMapping (matches FEAT-002 findings). No operator/exposure changed anywhere, so no before/after justification pair was required; no blow-out means no NeutralToneMapping switch was needed. Chef-is-FBX-not-VRM discrepancy re-recorded.

ONE SHARED QUALITY CONCEPT confirmed by grep: all four *Scene.tsx import @/components/three/quality; all four wrappers (CoachChatbot/ChefChatbot/WardrobeBuilder/VirtualPet) import the same module + the same QualityToggle. No per-scene ad-hoc widget.

VERIFICATION: npm run lint clean (only expected @next/next/no-page-custom-font warning, 0 errors); npm run build static export succeeds, all 5 pages prerender. git status confirms no out/ node_modules/ .next/ assets-src/ staged and docs/perf/ untouched. Committed docs/visual/ AFTER artifacts + AFTER.md + the two measurement-only harness flags on branch visual/lighting-quality. NOT pushed (per instructions). Left the unrelated untracked .agents/tasks/task-pet-motion-gallery + task-virtual-pet dirs out of the commit.
